name: Hereditary Hemolytic Anemia Due to Glucosephosphate Isomerase Deficiency

criteria.description: Reduced glucosephosphate isomerase enzyme activity in erythrocytes
Chronic hemolytic anemia with reticulocytosis and elevated indirect bilirubin
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the GPI gene
Exclusion of other common causes of hemolytic anemia (e.g., G6PD deficiency, pyruvate kinase deficiency)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic hemolytic anemia with reduced GPI enzyme activity and identification of pathogenic GPI gene mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires combination of biochemical enzyme assay and molecular genetic confirmation

searchTerms: long-term anemia with red cell breakdown

laboratory: Decreased GPI enzyme activity in red blood cells
Anemia with normocytic or slightly macrocytic indices
Peripheral blood smear showing hemolytic features without spherocytes
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the GPI gene (chromosome 19q13.1)
other: Exclusion of other hemolytic anemias by enzyme assays and molecular testing

distinguishingFeatures: Episodes of acute hemolysis triggered by oxidative stress
Similar chronic hemolytic anemia but different enzyme defect
Presence of spherocytes on peripheral smear
Defects in red cell membrane proteins

redFlags: Sudden worsening of hemolysis with infection or stress
Signs of iron overload or organ damage
